title: Losing 100 Billion and Still Ringing the Bell: The Compute Bill Behind Anthropic's Record IPO
excerpt: On November 19, Anthropic, less than six years after its founding, listed on Nasdaq (ticker: ANT), raising about $81.3 billion and setting the record for the la
content_html:
On November 19, Anthropic, less than six years after its founding, listed on Nasdaq (ticker: ANT), raising about $81.3 billion and setting the record for the largest IPO in history. It priced at $83 a share, closed its first day at $97.17, up 17.07%, with a market value of about $1.28 trillion and reaching $2 trillion at one point during the session; together with a $26 billion private placement, it raised about $107.3 billion in total.

$900 Billion Compute Commitment Looms Over $81 Billion ARR

Even more striking in the prospectus is another set of numbers: a net loss of more than $104 billion in the first nine months, but $94.3 billion of that was just a change in the fair value of liabilities, not actual spending; the operating loss was actually $1.26 billion. What truly hangs over it is $900.9 billion in long-term compute commitments, with $70.7 billion due within one year; as of the end of October, ARR was $81 billion. CEO Amodei calls compute “the deepest business problem,” and the approach is to buy less at first and add more as demand rises.

On the Subscription List, Half Are Backers, Half Are Rivals

Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC subscribed to the $26 billion private placement—all of them its chip or cloud suppliers—with Google and Nvidia each contributing $10 billion. But the prospectus also acknowledges that Amazon, Google, and Microsoft are both shareholders and competitors: on the eve of the IPO, Google cut Gemini 4 Carbon to $2 per million input tokens, compared with $8 for Fable 5.2; Microsoft's MAI Code 2 claims to achieve 96% of Opus 5.5's coding performance at 5% of the price. Suppliers' pocketbooks and rivals' price war are tangled together on the same list—this is precisely its most unusual position.
